summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and severe chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for evaluation of fever and a transient headache. He had recently been discharged after an ICU admission for RSV pneumonia and was on immunosuppressive therapy including prednisone, ruxolitinib, and sirolimus. Workup included CT imaging of the head and chest, which showed no acute intracranial process but possible sinusitis, and improved lung findings with new peribronchial nodules raising concern for recurrent infection. All cultures, including blood, urine, and respiratory viral panels, were negative. The patient remained afebrile throughout the admission. Posaconazole was restarted due to stable liver function, and IV antibiotics were de-escalated to oral amoxicillin. A new T3 compression fracture was identified, prompting recommendations for endocrine follow-up for osteoporosis. The patient was discharged home in stable condition on his baseline immunosuppressive regimen with plans for outpatient follow-up in infectious disease, transplant, and endocrinology.
